indexed10y.label: Australian Government indexed (CPI-linked) bond real yield, 10 years (interpolated)

breakeven10yBasis: Derived: F2 nominal 10-year yield minus F2 indexed 10-year real yield on the same date. Both are interpolated yields to maturity, not zero-coupon rates.
notes: Curves are RBA F17 fitted nominal zero-coupon yields, continuously compounded, from 0.25 to 10 years (F17 does not extend beyond 10 years). The 0-year F17 column, which tracks the cash rate, is omitted. Every business day is kept from 2023-09-28; earlier dates back to January 2017 are thinned to the last observation of each month. Missing values remain null; non-trading dates are excluded.

Publication lags differ: F17 is published monthly with daily data to the previous month-end (up to about five weeks old), while F2 is published weekly with daily data to a few business days earlier. asOf refers to the F17 curve; benchmarksAsOf refers to F2.

The RBA does not publish a real (inflation-indexed) zero-coupon curve. The real-yield curve is the F16 indicative yield to maturity of each Treasury Indexed Bond with at least 1 year to run, plotted at its time to maturity on the same dates as the nominal curve. Each breakeven is the nominal yield interpolated linearly between the two Treasury Bonds maturing either side of that indexed bond, minus its real yield; indexed bonds beyond the longest or before the shortest nominal bond have no breakeven. These are yields to maturity on bonds with different coupon, compounding and CPI-indexation conventions, so breakevens are approximate measures of CPI inflation compensation, including inflation risk and relative liquidity premia, not inflation forecasts. Shorter indexed bonds are omitted because the CPI indexation lag dominates their yields.

breakeven10y is kept for continuity: it is a dashboard calculation: the F2 interpolated 10-year nominal bond yield minus the F2 interpolated 10-year indexed bond real yield, on matching dates only, with no interpolation. Because these are yields to maturity on bonds with different coupon, compounding and CPI-indexation conventions, it is not a zero-coupon breakeven; it reflects CPI-linked inflation compensation including inflation risk and relative liquidity premia, not an inflation forecast.

The RBA describes these yields as its own assessments intended for research, which may be revised; they are not benchmarks for regulatory or commercial use. Observation dates are not publication or retrieval dates.
